items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Lonnie Johnson was on guitar on a session; Interviewee does not confirm or deny knowledge of Lonnie Johnson, only discusses Eddie Condon.

ctx.x: You got paid whatever you were promised. Sometimes you got it, sometimes you didn't. But what you got, that was for your record. And that was the end of your record, as far as you were concerned. You got paid for making a record and that was it. No bonus, no nothin', no... Now, the rest of it, that's between the leader, the leader of the band or the star or the big-shots, between them... It had nothing to do with the musicians. The musicians just made the date, and got their little salary, whatever they was…
Now, in the discography, it's mentioned that Eddie Condon was on banjo and Lonnie Johnson was on guitar on this "I Can't Give You Anything But Love" session. Do you remember Eddie Condon being there?

Yeah, he was... Well, he was in the studio every time Pops was. He was in the studio. You know what I mean? Yeah, he was the studio every time Pops made a record. Not only him, all his boys. Oh, there was a bunch of them. Mezz Mezzrow, you know, the Reefer King? Yeah, he was there. All them boys. They used to follow him around
